description.fun: The ghost of a creature that lived in the ancient seas, Dreepy still wanders its old haunts and bites at Clauncher out of habit. On its own it's so weak that a child could beat it, but with friends to train with, it grows strong. In the evening, flocks of Dreepy zoom over the sea poking other Pokémon. A real spider, Phrynarachne dreepy, is named after its triangular head.
description.guide: A Dragon and Ghost-type Pokémon, the spirit of a creature from ancient seas. Dreepy is weak on its own and evolves into Drakloak and then Dragapult.
description.tagline: A tiny prehistoric ghost that loves being launched

description.fun: A babysitter that flies at over 200 km/h with a Dreepy riding on its head, caring for it and fighting alongside it until it's grown up. Without a Dreepy to look after, it gets so uneasy that it'll try to adopt any Pokémon it finds instead. But lose a battle, and its Dreepy wanders off without a second thought.
description.guide: The middle stage of Dreepy's line, a Dragon and Ghost-type Pokémon that carries a Dreepy on its head and looks after it. It is the only Pokémon that evolves starting at level 60.
description.tagline: A flying babysitter that can't stand an empty head

description.fun: Shaped like a stealth bomber, Dragapult keeps Dreepy in the holes in its horns and launches them like supersonic missiles once a fight starts, and the Dreepy can't wait for their turn. By clearing its mind it can turn its whole body transparent, Dreepy and all. In the 2020 Pokémon of the Year poll it was voted the most popular Pokémon from Sword and Shield.
description.guide: The final evolution of Dreepy, a Dragon and Ghost-type Pokémon that fires Dreepy from its horns and can turn invisible. It was voted the most popular Generation VIII Pokémon in the 2020 Pokémon of the Year poll.
description.tagline: A stealth dragon that launches its babies like missiles
